text:
Mike A (AP): Hey team — DataCraft (vendor) submitted an invoice marked 0% VAT with a DE VAT ID. They also attached a statement saying reverse charge applies. Can someone confirm we can pay net or do we need to withhold/gross-up?

Elena F (Tax): Share the VAT ID and the invoice PDF. If they're EU-registered and we’re buying B2B services, reverse charge might be fine — but need to validate their VAT ID in VIES. Also check whether the service is place-of-supply in DE vs our country.

Mike A (AP): VAT ID: DE999999999. Invoice attached in the thread (invoice_8923.pdf). They invoiced from Berlin.

Priya S (Finance Ops): Quick note — payment is scheduled for EOM but I put it on hold until tax confirm. If reverse charge is valid we won’t add VAT. If not, we need VAT charged or consider gross-up?

Jasper (AE): Vendor says they’re EU company, not US. They included a US W-9 accidentally in the portal when we asked for tax docs. I flagged it. They said they’re not US.

Elena F (Tax): W-9/W-8 are for US withholding only — irrelevant for EU VAT. For EU vendors we need a valid VAT number and evidence of B2B supply. I’ll run VIES check now.

TaxBot: VIES lookup for DE999999999 — result: "INVALID". 

Elena F (Tax): Hmm VIES returned invalid. Could be formatting or temporary outage. Mike, can you confirm the VAT ID exactly as on their invoice (spaces, country code)? Also ask vendor for their VAT registration certificate (un-redacted) or a screenshot of their national portal.

Mike A (AP): Sent vendor 2x requests asking for: 1) copy of VAT registration cert, 2) confirmation that the supply is B2B to Redwood (we're EU-based billing entity). They replied with a scanned letter but the number on the letter is DE 99 999 999 9 (with spaces) — I pasted exactly earlier.

Priya S (Finance Ops): If they can’t validate, we should either: a) ask them to reissue with German VAT charged, or b) we withhold VAT? What’s the withholding rule for services from DE vendor to Redwoods EU entity?

Elena F (Tax): Withholding isn’t the mechanism for VAT. If reverse charge doesn't apply we must pay VAT on the invoice. Withholding relates to income tax (and usually W-8/W-9 for US vendors). So for VAT: either they charge VAT or provide proof of valid VAT and B2B status. If they can't provide, have them reissue with VAT included (we’ll reclaim via our VAT return?).

Jasper (AE): Vendor asks if Redwood can accept a gross-up (i.e., we increase payment to cover extra VAT) — they say it’s quicker than reissuing. Any objections?

Elena F (Tax): Gross-up is fine contractually if procurement/legal approve. But we must document tax treatment. Also gross-up increases our cost. Prefer vendor reissue with VAT if they can. If they insist, we need a PO amendment and sign-off from finance leadership.

Mike A (AP): OK — I pushed back asking for VAT cert and told them gross-up would need approval and a new invoice/PO.

Priya S (Finance Ops): For the record, if we gross-up: record the invoice net and an expense line for VAT paid, or record as VAT-inclusive cost? Need GL guidance from accounting team.

Elena F (Tax): Tagging accounting: @Priya S will collect GL guidance, but tax-wise we should avoid gross-ups unless necessary.

Mike A (AP): Vendor replied: they can provide national cert but number still shows as DE999999999. They asked if we can validate from our side and proceed.

Elena F (Tax): I'll try VIES again and then the German tax portal. If still unclear, request a screenshot of the registration portal with their name/company matching the invoice. If they refuse, require VAT-charged invoice.

Jasper (AE): Thanks, Elena. I’ll tell vendor to cooperate (they want the money in 7 days).

TaxBot: VIES lookup re-run: temporary service error. Suggested manual verification with national registry.

Mike A (AP): Noted. I'll extend payment window 7 days and keep on hold.

Priya S (Finance Ops): Tagging @Elena F for final sign-off when verified. Leaving a note in AP system: HOLD_TAX_VALIDATION.

Elena F (Tax): Final: if vendor supplies a scanned official cert showing company name and VAT ID matching invoice, approve release net (reverse charge). If not, require reissued invoice with German VAT or escalate to procurement for PO amendment for gross-up.

Mike A (AP): Got it. Will update thread when vendor responds. :thumbsup:
